cities.d: the administrative center; other countries maintain their embassies there.

x.around: Abidjan is quite spread out so walking can take a lot of time and bicycle riding isn't the safest choice (except nearer the water in Zone Quatre). However, there are many options to get around via motor transport.
x.intro: Serving as the capital from 1933 until 1983, Abidjan is the biggest and most important city of Cote d'Ivoire. With a population of around 4,000,000 people, it is the second largest city in West Africa after Lagos and has historically been the economic power base of the region.

must.d: A 30 km² national park just north of Abidjan featuring many tropical rare woods (mahogany, avodirés, waffle wood and more). There are several walking paths and popular for trekking.

n.es: Biblioteca nacional de Costa de Marfil

must.d: The national museum of Côte d'Ivoire, first opened in 1942. Contains substantial archaeological and ethological collections, making it one of the most important museums in the region.

n.en: Museum of Civilizations in Côte d'Ivoire
n.fr: musée des civilisations de Côte d'Ivoire

next.d: A small town three hours north where you can have an audience with the king of Indénié Kingdom.
The second largest city of Côte d'Ivoire located in the dead center of the country with a lively market and night scene.
About 45 minutes to the east and the original capital of the country with old Colonial architecture that is being restored and an excellent beach.
An old town about six hours west of Abidjan with nice beaches which serves as a secondary port city for the country.

x.safe: There are a number of issues that plague Abidjan, which are indicative of the overall problems that Cote d'Ivoire is experiencing. First and foremost are the military checkpoints. While generally harmless for foreigners, they can make it maddening to get across the city in a timely fashion, especially if one is in a private car. Bribes are commonplace, but not an absolute. Carrying small bills is always a good idea.

cities.d: although it has been the capital since 1983, it is not the administrative centre.

hidden.d: Much smaller cathedral in the city centre.

n.es: Catedral de San Agustín de Yamoussoukro

x.intro: Yamoussoukro is the capital of Côte d'Ivoire and is perhaps the single most bizarre modern city on Earth. It is a large grid of paved streets and lights with almost nothing at all in between them. It would seem that former President Felix Houphouet-Boigny's dream that his home town would become a busy capital city never came to fruition. The streets are now potholed, the lights no longer work and the jungle is reclaiming them in places. Nevertheless "Yam" is worth a visit.

n.en: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
n.es: basílica de Nuestra Señora de la Paz de Yamusukro
n.it: basilica di Nostra Signora della Pace

cities.d: home of the Senoufo people and culture, bursts with commerce during Feb–May because of flowing cotton and cashew trade.

x.around: Taxi-Moto take you anywhere in and outside Korhogo. Short rides (up to 2km) usually cost 300-500 CFA.
x.intro: Korhogo is the capital of the Savanes District a city in the northern part of the Côte d'Ivoire, also known as the Northern Savanna. Several of the UNESCO World Heritage Sudanese-style mosques of Côte d'Ivoire are in the district or nearby.
Bouaké is Cote d'Ivoire's second-largest city, located in the Eastern Plantations region.

must.d: Seat of the archdiose, this cathedral is constructed in a brutalist architectural style.

n.en: St. Teresa of Infant Jesus Cathedral

x.around: Shared taxis go between the city centre and the seaside maquis area for 200 CFA per passenger. Foreigners will be told the price is 1000 but tell the driver that you know the local rate is 200.
x.intro: San-Pédro is a city of 260,000 in Southwestern Forests region of Côte d'Ivoire and the nation's second largest port.

cities.d: a coastal town full of colonial charm, often a retreat for local Ivorians seeking to escape the city life of Abidjan on the weekends.

x.around: The town is largely divided into two distinct halves. On the south side of the Ébrié Lagoon is Ancien Bassam, the old French town where most of the colonial buildings and attractions are located. Nouveau Bassam lies to the north of the lagoon, and grew out of the old servant quarters to become the main business centre. The two are connected by a small bridge.

hidden.d: Beautiful house of worship built by the French in 1910, renovated in 2004.
An elegant building that has also been restored. It no longer functions as a post office.

Unlike some other buildings, the name of this colourful building describes what it's used for. In this "house of the artists" you can watch local sculptors and other artists working and buy their creations.
Constructed in 1910, it was used as a court until 1954. This building has not been as lucky as the other French colonial structures, and has reportedly decayed beyond repair.

The seaside of Ancien Bassam is extremely popular among Ivorians. On the weekends, the place is packed, however, during the weekdays, you may have it all to yourself. Beware of strong currents; there are no lifeguards.
After tourism, ceramics are probably Grand-Bassam's biggest industry. This is a museum of Ivorian traditional ceramic and an exhibition hall for the works of local artisans..

x.intro: Filled to the brim with French colonial charm, Grand-Bassam is a town in the Lagunes region of Côte d'Ivoire.

next.d: The country's economic capital is only a short drive down the road.
Another beach town that is popular among locals.

intro: Côte d'Ivoire (Ivory Coast) is a country in West Africa, visited for its beaches, rainforest, wildlife and tourist villages. Resort lodgings in coastal areas draw many visitors.

x.intro: For the national park in South Island, see Westland Tai Poutini National Park Taï National Park is in Côte d'Ivoire, in the southwest of the country about 100 km in from the coast and near the Liberian border.
x.safe: This forest area is a natural reservoir of the Ebola virus. This is spread by contact with excretions or bodily fluids of infected animals or humans and the main defense is rigorous hygiene. As of 2022, three vaccines have been approved for humans. Consult a doctor for details if planning a trip.

n.es: Reserva natural integral del Monte Nimba
n.fr: réserve naturelle intégrale du Mont Nimba
n.it: Riserva naturale integrale del Monte Nimba

x.intro: Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve covers parts of Côte d'Ivoire and Guinea. It is an endangered UNESCO World Heritage Site. The reserve covers significant portions of the Nimba Range, a geographically unique area with unusually rich flora and fauna, including exceptional numbers of single-site endemic species, such as viviparous toads, and horseshoe bats. Its highest peak is Mount Richard-Molard at 1,752 m (5,750 ft), which is the highest peak of both countries.
